rows.proof: `FY2012 COLLECTION OF TAXES`, PDF page 78 of the FY2012 annual town report (4118-fy-2012-annual-town-report.pdf), printed folio 75 -- the Collector's receivable control, every tax year still open at 30 June 2012. EVERY PAGE OF THIS REPORT IS A PHOTOGRAPH -- pdfplumber returns 0 words on all 116 pages, tested per page -- so it was read off the page's OWN stored bitmap; NO recognition was used. THE PAGE IS BOUND UPSIDE DOWN in the PDF. THE PRINTED COLUMN HEADER, READ OFF THE PAGE AND WRITTEN DOWN (rule 13b.4), is `COLLECTION OF TAXES` | `FORWARD` | `COMMITTMENTS` | `ADJUSTMENTS` | `REFUNDS` | `PAYMENTS` | `ABATEMENTS` | `TRANSFER` | `BALANCES` -- `COMMITTMENTS` is the page's own spelling and is kept. SIGNS ARE THE PAGE'S, NOT OURS: payments, abatements and most transfers print in parentheses and are stored negative; a few transfers and adjustments print positive and are stored positive. Nothing was negated to make an identity work, which is why the identity is a plain SUM. THE PAGE IS ROTATED AND THAT COST TWO WRONG READINGS BEFORE IT WAS MEASURED (rule 13b.1). At full-page scale the right-hand columns appear one row below their labels in the first third of the table and level with them in the middle, and reading either way produces rows that do not close. A correlation of the left and right row profiles returned -58 pixels, which is WRONG: the row grid is periodic at about 42 pixels, so the correlation peak is ambiguous by whole rows and it landed on the wrong one, and deskewing by it made the stagger three rows instead of one. The rotation was then taken from the page itself -- the printed header words descend from `FORWARD` to `BALANCES` by about one row pitch across 2,800 pixels, so +0.86 degrees -- and at that angle the header is level and every row lines up with its own figures. WHAT PROVES IT, and it is two independent things: all EIGHT columns foot to the printed GRAND TOTAL exactly, no tolerance declared (1,582,075.89 / 21,632,937.46 / -25,896.76 / 59,113.15 / -21,098,279.80 / -146,382.54 / -352,631.10 / 1,650,936.30); and all 53 rows close on the identity the page states about each of them, declared here as a `check` row. A wrong deskew cannot make 53 real row identities and 8 column totals close at once. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: a balance carried is tax COMMITTED and not collected, which is not the same as tax owed by anyone still reachable -- some of these years are fifteen years old. Nothing here says what was written off, and the page prints no allowance for uncollectible accounts.

rows.proof: `FY 2013 Omnibus Budget`, PDF pages 81-82 of the FY2012 annual town report (4118-fy-2012-annual-town-report.pdf), printed folios 78-79 -- the budget Town Meeting VOTED under Article 8, printed inside the FY2012 report. EVERY PAGE OF THIS REPORT IS A PHOTOGRAPH -- pdfplumber returns 0 words on all 116 pages, tested per page -- so it was read off the pages' own 518 dpi bitmaps; NO recognition was used. THE PRINTED COLUMN HEADER, READ OFF THE PAGE AND WRITTEN DOWN (rule 13b.4), is `Line No.` | `Account` | `VOTED FY 2013`. ONE money column. `$  -` is the page's explicit zero and is recorded as 0.00. The line numbering runs 1 to 83 with 3A, 3B, 13A, 14A, 46A, 64A, 68A and 79A inserted and NO line 18 -- that is what the page prints. THIS IS A VOTE, NOT A LEDGER: `VOTED FY 2013` is what Town Meeting appropriated for the NEXT fiscal year, so it belongs to FY2013 and must never be added to the FY2012 appropriations schedule on pp.60-65, which reports what FY2012 spent. WHAT PROVES IT: the page prints a subtotal for every section and the lines foot to it exactly, section by section, with no tolerance declared. Each section is its own group in `page-reads/` so that each of those totals is a check a script runs rather than a sentence. THE TOWN'S OWN TOTAL DOES NOT FOOT, and that is attested rather than mended: the eleven printed section totals sum to 27,488,841.00 and `Total Omnibus` prints 27,489,441.00, SIX HUNDRED DOLLARS more. The reading is not in doubt -- every one of the eleven sections closes on its own printed subtotal from its own printed lines, which is eleven independent checks on the components, and `Total Omnibus` was re-read upright at full scale. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: which figure is wrong. The $600 could be a line the page does not print, a section total understated, or the grand total overstated, and nothing on these two pages distinguishes them. Nothing here picks a digit to make it close (rule 14). SECTION: Maturing Debt & Interest.
